content: The Blood Pressure Association (BPA) is a charitable organization based in the United Kingdom, established in October 2000. Its primary mission is to provide comprehensive information and support to individuals diagnosed with high blood pressure, also known as hypertension. Additionally, the organization aims to educate the general public about the critical role blood pressure plays in overall health and well-being. The BPA offers free information packs to anyone in the UK upon request. These packs contain detailed guidance on high blood pressure and strategies to effectively lower it. Furthermore, the organization provides free membership to all UK residents, granting them full access to the BPA's extensive information services. Every year, during the second week of September, the BPA organizes an event called Know Your Numbers Week. During this initiative, healthcare professionals, including doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and trained personnel, provide free blood pressure testing services. These tests are conducted in various locations across the UK, such as hospitals, pharmacies, health centers, and shopping centers. The BPA also publishes a quarterly subscription magazine titled Positive Pressure, which contains articles and resources related to blood pressure management and health. The patron of the Blood Pressure Association is Sir David Attenborough, a renowned broadcaster and naturalist.
